before: {{sibling}} refuses the proposal and the relationship deteriorates. You keep the goods, together with the saw’s excellent negotiating reputation.
after: {{sibling}} sits on the bed to end the demonstration. You are left holding a saw and the much smaller half of the conversation.

before: You publicly challenge the scheme. Your reputation rises while {{other}} acquires a specific grievance against you.
after: {{other}} spends supper explaining why nobody should believe you. The explanation repeats your warning to everyone who missed it.

before: {{other}} discovers the error in public. Your reputation for wit rises slightly; your reputation with the singer falls considerably.
after: The street demands the refrain. {{other}} discovers that a love song can carry a name much farther when the person named wishes it would stop.

before: You bring the demand into public view. Your reputation rises and {{other}} becomes a named rival rather than an invisible expense.
after: You invite the neighbours to inspect the shade. {{other}} objects to so many people standing in an asset they have not paid to admire.

before: The line vanishes before another copy can be compared. You keep the secret and gain {{other}}’s trust in your willingness to cross a boundary.
after: The stain vanishes. {{other}} admires the clean sleeve with the uncomfortable warmth of someone who now knows exactly what you will wash for a friend.

before: You keep the purse’s contents and leave the boot where it will be found. {{other}} knows enough to make the money less comfortable than it feels.
after: Eight gold comes out of the boot. {{other}} watches you return the empty footwear with a helpfulness that is going to require explaining later.

before: Your standing in the guild improves when you refuse. {{other}} looks for a craftsman whose signature is more flexible than the wood.
after: {{other}} searches for another maker willing to promise that the missing drink is merely hiding somewhere very respectable. Your tools remain unemployed and your mark remains yours.

before: You earn nine gold and gain a fraud complaint. The moths prove more candid witnesses than your description.
after: The buyer pays nine gold. A moth emerges during your description of the wool’s excellent health and supplies a much shorter opinion.

before: You force the proposed change into the open. Your reputation and experience rise; the secret fee disappears.
after: You read the missing word aloud. {{other}} has to swallow the fee along with an objection that sounds considerably worse when everyone can hear it.

before: The accusation is treated as a deliberate falsehood. You lose your employment and are imprisoned for the performance.
after: The patron stops knowing you halfway through the last verse. You lose the post and gain a cell, where the audience is smaller and the acoustics regrettably good.

before: You turn the proposed risk back toward its owner. Your reputation rises; {{other}} declines the opportunity to become the subject.
after: You offer to put {{other}} in the heroic part. The proposed song becomes unsuitable for performance with astonishing speed.

before: You earn thirteen gold and create a supply-fraud charge. The evidence walks badly but reaches the clerk.
after: Thirteen gold changes hands. The first boot comes apart on the way to inspection, leaving its owner to deliver the complaint barefoot.

before: The compliment reaches {{other}} a moment late. You gain charm and lose a little trust in the room.
after: {{other}} smiles before understanding the compliment. The smile retreats very carefully, as though nobody has seen where it was standing.

before: You pay ten gold for a conspicuous seat, not an office. Your family’s reputation rises slightly; the council seals stay with their holders.
after: Ten gold buys you a chair so conspicuous that nobody can overlook your lack of a seal. Your relatives arrive early to admire the upholstery.

before: You gain standing for refusing a blank commitment. {{other}} must interrupt the urgency long enough to say what it is for.
after: {{other}} explains that delay will imperil the peace. You ask which peace. This produces the first useful pause of the meeting.

before: You gain Church standing and lose hunting favour with {{other}}. The altar keeps the quieter congregation.
after: You lead the hunt away. {{other}} complains about losing the trail to someone who has just acquired an excellent reason to stop listening.

before: You pay five gold for an unverified rumour. No actual secret is revealed merely because someone priced it as one.
after: For five gold, {{other}} leans close enough to repeat something you heard yesterday. The improved intimacy appears to be the expensive part.

before: You pay for alteration rather than for endurance. {{other}} admires the result without admitting it needed work.
after: The armourer releases the extra inch. {{other}} praises your noble bearing without asking why it has suddenly become possible to sit down.

before: You improve Crown standing by asking for lawful confirmation. {{other}} dislikes the number of adults now reading the order.
after: The adults read the order together. {{other}} discovers that a child’s impressive signature has acquired rather too many people who know how the child writes.

before: You gain public standing and lose favour with {{other}}. Your doors remain useful for entering as well as leaving.
after: Your guest leaves by the front door. {{other}} watches a perfectly serviceable ransom walk away under its own power.

before: You gain standing and anger {{other}} by distinguishing a claim from geography.
after: You take the drawing outside. The river provides a comparison so persuasive that {{other}} begins objecting to the weather instead.

before: You pay for the correction and improve your household’s public standing. {{other}} thanks you for solving the argument before it needed a wound.
after: You pay for new cloth before anyone draws a sword. {{other}} thanks you, then asks the tailor to show the design upright twice before cutting.

before: You damage public order and create a lasting family feud with {{other}} over the deliberate provocation.
after: {{other}} takes the insult home. By supper both families can describe the colours perfectly and the original reason for using them much less clearly.

before: You improve Crown standing and offend {{other}}. The force becomes smaller on paper and no smaller in the field.
after: The imaginary ranks are dismissed without pay. {{other}} is left commanding exactly as many people as can hear the order.

before: You improve trust with {{other}}. The households do not acquire an alliance merely because the drinking is less hostile.
after: {{other}} finally drinks without waiting to see whether you do first. The cups have accomplished a modest amount of work for such small objects.

before: You gain a little charm and deepen the rivalry. {{other}} now has a sentence worth repeating accurately.
after: {{other}} spends the evening explaining that the insult caused no offence. Before midnight the kitchen can repeat it word for word.

before: You expose the weak account without inventing a miracle. Your reputation improves and {{other}} becomes less welcoming to questions.
after: {{other}} moves the smaller skull behind the larger one. The saint has become considerably older in the time it takes to ask one question.

before: Your household gives up food and gains reputation. {{other}} sees a donation delivered without first hearing its name.
after: The food reaches the hungry before {{other}} can announce the giver. For once, the chewing gets to interrupt the important names.

before: You gain understanding without demanding a sign. {{other}} is less annoyed once no one is watching the disappointment.
after: You sit quietly long enough for {{other}} to stop performing silence at you. The remainder of the afternoon becomes much more peaceful.

before: You gain a little health by resting. Any existing eye condition remains; the spoon’s recovery proves nothing about yours.
after: You rest your eyes while the spoon receives its second treatment. {{other}} appears disappointed that the healthier patient has no money of its own.

before: You pay for help and recover some strength without pretending the payment itself removes the disease.
after: Seven gold hires another pair of hands. From bed you listen to the work continue without requiring your fever to show any professional enthusiasm.

before: The ferry reaches the bank. You gain a small reputation for nerve and remain unable to spend it on better buoyancy.
after: The ferry reaches the bank. The ferryman praises your courage while standing on a part of the boat he refused to share during the crossing.

before: You pay to leave a bundle behind. The ferryman reluctantly accepts that cargo can survive the inconvenience of missing a crossing.
after: The bundle stays ashore. {{other}} discovers that a boat can become less profitable and much more convincing at the same time.

before: You lose work performance and gain trust with {{other}} by refusing a useful falsehood. Your health remains a fact rather than a certificate.
after: You explain what you can actually lift. {{other}} stops rehearsing the recovery and helps move the work to someone capable of standing beside it.

before: You gain a little health and a trustworthy bond. The wound remains under care rather than vanishing under a promise.
after: You promise a useful afternoon when you are well. {{other}} ties the bandage without testing whether gratitude needs to be quite so tight.

before: You learn something about its scale and improve your bond with {{other}}. The bone remains remarkable without an extra power.
after: You spend an hour examining the enormous bone. {{other}} keeps interrupting to mention luck, which proves much harder to point to than the joints.

before: You damage {{other}}’s trust and lose public standing for turning an unpaid wage into a moral failing.
after: The crowd asks why the devil should work for nothing. {{other}} has to defend a play in which the villain has become the most reasonable person present.

before: You gain practical experience and a warm bond with {{other}}. An evening passes without anybody trying to conquer anything.
after: {{other}} opens the tiny gates and shows you the hinges. Nobody besieges anything; two people spend an excellent evening admiring a door.

before: Your guild contact finds the exemption. The household keeps its fee.
after: The guild contact finds the exemption. The collector departs without the fee and with a much lower opinion of children being taught to read.

before: Your household contact quotes the service oath. You receive bread and an enemy in the stores.
after: Your household receives its bread. The stores clerk hands over each loaf as though personally surrendering a small fort.

before: The family record settles precedence without an insult. Your cousin has less reason to press another grievance.
after: The cousin receives the proper seat. It is less comfortable than the disputed one, but much harder to call an outrage.

before: The modest sample gives the workshop a place at the feast without emptying its supper pot.
after: The workshop’s sample is admired, tasted and promptly requested in a larger quantity. Your household still has supper when the important guests finish theirs.

before: The shared lesson gives the guards no wager to collect. Your guardian records a rare quiet agreement between heirs.
after: The guards return their wagers and watch both heirs share a lesson. Nobody is willing to bet on the peace lasting, but the lesson gets finished.

before: You drive the rat out and repair the gap, losing a little blood to the work. Household stores and security improve under a watchman that is now a plank.
after: The rat departs through the gap just before you close it. Your new watchman is a plank: silent, dependable and completely uninterested in the grain.

before: You unhorse the opponent and earn a net eight gold after the entry fee. The steward objects only to how many people saw the small horse win.
after: The small horse wins. The steward hands over your net eight gold while studying the animal for evidence of a more respectable size.

before: You admit the truth and gain faith. The admission does not settle debts or erase charges; it merely stops the priest waiting for the missing part.
after: The priest finally hears the missing part. He stops waiting for it and starts giving advice, which you find considerably less comfortable than the silence.

before: You gain two gold. {{peer}} learns exactly which sort of mistake you prefer not to correct.
after: You pocket the extra coins. {{peer}} asks whether your arithmetic always improves when someone else is paying.

before: You gain food and lose the advantage of a simple explanation. {{carer}} puts both signatures beside you at supper.
after: The extra food reaches supper before your explanation. {{carer}} puts both signatures beside your bowl and waits for you to discover which one you wrote.

before: You earn eight gold for arranging an unusually exclusive alphabet. {{other}} calls the result historically inevitable.
after: The payer’s titles go all the way round the bell. Eight gold buys you the excellent opinion of someone now able to hear their own importance every hour.

before: You earn the wage while your own stores suffer. {{other}} records your absence with rather more enthusiasm than your presence ever received.
after: You return with a wage and find your own stores emptier. {{other}} congratulates you on being so industrious somewhere else.

before: You earn twelve gold. {{other}} submits the hours, which look much longer when laid beside your signature.
after: Twelve gold reaches your purse. The apprentices reach the clerk before dawn, for once making excellent use of the hours you insisted were still afternoon.

before: Your household gains twenty gold. The tenants learn that silence is the cheapest answer, and {{other}} begins bringing shorter rolls with larger totals.
after: Twenty gold reaches the household. The tenants stop answering questions freely, having learned what an answer costs in your chair.
